Kreplach for Yom Kippur

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Serves 6-8 (makes about 30-40 kreplach)Prep 60 minCook 20 min

Kreplach, small, savory dumplings, are a beloved dish often served as part of the pre-fast meal before Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement. Traditionally filled with seasoned ground meat and served in clear chicken soup, they offer a comforting and substantial meal to prepare for the solemn fast ahead. The "hidden" filling is sometimes seen as a symbol of hidden sins or the concealed nature of divine mercy.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (240g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, divided
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) cold water
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 1/2 pound (225g) ground beef or chicken
  • 1 large egg, for filling
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 6 cups (1.4 liters) prepared chicken broth, for serving

Method

  1. To make the dough: In a large bowl, combine the flour and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Make a well in the center and add the 2 large eggs and cold water. Mix with a fork until a shaggy dough forms, then turn out onto a lightly floured surface.
  2. Knead the dough for 8-10 minutes, or until it is smooth and elastic. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
  3. To make the filling: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
  4. Add the ground meat to the skillet and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat and let the mixture cool completely.
  5. Once cooled, transfer the meat mixture to a bowl. Add the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, the 1 large egg, and black pepper. Mix well to combine.
  6. To assemble the kreplach: Divide the dough into two or three portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one portion of dough very thinly, about 1/16 inch (1.5mm) thick.
  7. Using a 2-3 inch (5-7.5 cm) round cookie cutter or a knife, cut the dough into circles or squares. Place about 1 teaspoon of the meat filling in the center of each dough piece.
  8. Fold the dough over the filling to create a half-moon shape (for circles) or a triangle (for squares). Pinch the edges firmly to seal, ensuring no filling can escape. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
  9. Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully add the kreplach in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot.
  10. Cook the kreplach for 5-8 minutes, or until they float to the surface and are tender. Remove with a slotted spoon.
  11. Serve the cooked kreplach immediately in bowls of hot chicken broth.

Tips

  • For make-ahead convenience, cooked kreplach can be frozen. Arrange them in a single layer on a baking sheet until solid, then transfer to a freezer-safe bag for up to 3 months. Reheat directly from frozen in hot broth.
  • Ensure the dough is rolled very thin; this is key to tender kreplach. If the dough is too thick, the dumplings will be heavy.
  • For a dairy meal (not traditional for pre-Yom Kippur fast, but a variation), you can fill kreplach with mashed potatoes or a cheese mixture (e.g., ricotta, egg, salt, pepper).
